rel_l2_note: verify.py gates on l2_norm_passed (all 5 seeds true) but does not surface the numeric rel-L2 in its summary; expected ~1.5e-5 by analogy to the fp32 siblings (add_rmsnorm_matmul_v1 1.46e-5), ~1.37x under the 2e-5 gate
structure: raw-2D self-slicing (identity transform_to_nki_inputs); M-outer; per-M-tile: identity nc_matmul transpose of 16 [128,128] x K-sub-tiles -> xT[k_in,m_in]; N-chunk GEMM loop (4 chunks, K-accumulate 16 tiles into [128,512] fp32 PSUM) then acc+z_tile into a full [128,2048] y SBUF buffer (residual add before norm); single fused RMSNorm over N (square -> separate sq temp -> single full-2048 free-axis tensor_reduce(axis=[1]) -> mean_eps = sumsq*(1/N)+eps two-op tensor_scalar -> rsqrt); output scale out = (y*inv_rms) then *g_bcast applied FULL-WIDTH over the [128,2048] row in 2 ops + a single store (reads the still-live y; NO PSUM constraint on the elementwise output); all-w-resident (16 tiles [128,2048], 128KB/part) loaded ONCE before the M-loop
eps_form: SAFE: mean_eps = sumsq*(1/N) + eps (two-op tensor_scalar, eps added AFTER /N mean, matches reference np.mean(y**2,axis=-1)+eps); NOT rsqrt((sumsq+eps)/N)
reduce_axis: over N free axis (axis=[1]) of the assembled [128,N] matmul output -- the MIRROR of the norm-first siblings which reduced over K
g_placement: length-N free/output axis -> [1,N] broadcast_to([128,N]) multiply on the output; NEVER folded into w (g does not sit on the contraction axis for this op)
output_store: full-width [128,N] (2 ops + 1 store) -- R1 A/B measured 6.4% faster than a per-512-chunk store (0.9612 vs 1.0221ms); the output is SBUF->SBUF elementwise with no PSUM-bank constraint so chunking only adds Vec/Scalar+store overhead
residency_path: full-w resident (primary path) -- succeeded, no fallback ladder triggered; HBMrd=84MB confirms single pass
notes: First correct Phase-1 kernel for matmul_add_rmsnorm. fp32 throughout, full 5-seed L2 PASS, 3.920x over the 3.768ms baseline (--fast 0.9612 / full5 0.9612 agree exactly). The dominant win is w-residency: HBMrd 84MB (single pass over x+w+z, ~80MB floor) vs the baseline's ~537MB of in-loop w reloads (32x re-stream of the 16MB weight). PE-bound at the fp32 systolic floor (PE=96% MFU=46%, matching siblings add_rmsnorm_matmul_v1 94% / rmsnorm_matmul_v1 97%); RMSNorm cheap/overlapped (Vec 15% Scl 9% DMA 20%); the 512 identity transposes hidden under the matmul. Built on the explicit nc_matmul + identity-transpose idiom so the Phase-2 compensated bf16x2 split is a localized extension, not a rewrite. Round-0 review flagged the output-store structure; R1 resolved it by measuring both correct variants and keeping the faster full-width store (see the per-chunk A/B reject node). Phase-2 opener: compensated bf16x2 split-matmul (beat the fp32 floor on every sibling; note the fp32 margin is ~1.37x, tighter headroom).

structure: identical to matmul_add_rmsnorm_v1 EXCEPT the output scale/store is a per-512-wide-chunk loop (for c in affine_range(4): out_sb[128,512] = tensor_scalar(y[:,chunk]*inv_rms) then *g[:,chunk] broadcast, store chunk) instead of the promoted full-width [128,N] store
notes: Round-1 A/B for the Round-0-review output-store question. Both variants PASS the full 5-seed gate and are HBMrd=84MB (identical residency). The output scale is pure SBUF->SBUF elementwise with NO PSUM-bank constraint (unlike the GEMM accumulator, chunked to 512 to fit one fp32 PSUM bank), so chunking it buys nothing and costs instruction overhead: 8 narrow Vec/Scalar ops + 4 stores/M-tile vs 2 full-width ops + 1 store, serializing the Vector Engine against the PE-bound matmul (PE 96->98%, MFU 46->43%). Confirms the full-width output store is the correct Phase-1 choice; the 512-wide chunking belongs on the PSUM-bounded GEMM accumulator, not the elementwise output. Kept as a first-class negative datum; NOT promoted. See profile/matmul_add_rmsnorm_v1_chunked_store_reject.txt

structure: zero-remote-spend numpy pre-check for the phase-2 compensated bf16x2 3-product split matmul. Reproduces the EXACT scored input (adapter np.random.seed(s) then draw x->w->z->g; z is (M,N), g is (N,) on the OUTPUT axes for this mirror op), the NKIBench fp32 reference, and an idealized RNE bf16x2 split (x_hi/x_lo, w_hi/w_lo; prod = x_hi@w_hi + x_hi@w_lo + x_lo@w_hi in exact fp32, drop lo@lo) then +z then the fp32 norm+scale epilogue.
key_result: This op is the MIRROR of the norm->GEMM siblings: the bf16 matmul error lands in y, and y feeds BOTH the norm (inv_rms) AND the output numerator -- a composite path the sibling sims never exercised (they post-scaled inv_rms computed from the exact fp32 activation). The sim measures that composite: fp32 control rel-L2 = 0.000e+00 (model exact); plain bf16 = 2.350e-3 (fails gate 117x, confirms single-limb is out); bf16x2 3-product WORST over 7 seeds = 4.454e-6 (~4.5x under the 2e-5 gate, ~3.3x below the sibling fp32 v1's own on-device 1.46e-5); 4-product = 3.491e-6 (sizes the dropped lo@lo term ~ negligible). Predicted DEVICE quadrature sqrt(1.46e-5^2 + 4.454e-6^2) = 1.526e-5 (matches the sibling's ACTUAL measured on-device bf16x2 rel-L2 1.528e-5) => ~1.31x under gate, comfortable. g is on the OUTPUT axis N here so it is NOT folded into w (folding g[n] into w[k,n] would scale y before the norm and break rms=sqrt(mean(y^2))); only ONE g placement to check.
notes: De-risks the phase-2 opener. worst bf16-only 4.454e-6 <= 1.5e-5 comfortably-below threshold; full-5-seed on-device still gates promotion. Evidence: profile/matmul_add_rmsnorm_offline_bf16_split_sim.txt. Mirror-op contrast to sibling offline_bf16_split_sim (which compared g-into-w vs g-on-act because its g was per-K contraction).

split_order: PINNED: weights w (fp32 FIRST) -> w_hi=bf16(w) -> w_res=w-w_hi (fp32 tensor_tensor) -> w_lo=bf16(w_res), split ONCE before the M-loop, resident [16,128,2048] bf16 limbs; activation xT=transpose(x) (exact fp32 identity nc_matmul) -> xT_hi=bf16(xT) -> xT_res=xT-xT_hi -> xT_lo=bf16(xT_res), split per transposed sub-tile
products: 3-product FIXED order: xT_hi@w_hi + xT_hi@w_lo + xT_lo@w_hi in one [128,512] fp32 PSUM bank (xT_lo@w_lo DROPPED); normal fp32 PSUM accumulation, no intermediate narrowing
eps_form: SAFE two-op mean_eps = sumsq*(1/N) + eps (eps AFTER /N mean)
g_placement: NOT folded: g on the OUTPUT free axis (N), applied [1,N]->[128,N] broadcast AFTER the norm (out=y*inv_rms*g); folding into w would scale y before the norm (algebraically wrong for this mirror op)
invariants: fp32 residual add y=x@w+z BEFORE the norm; fp32 RMSNorm reduction over N (square/tensor_reduce/mean_eps/rsqrt); inv_rms NOT commuted (norm reduces over N -> full [128,N] y assembled before inv_rms); full-width [128,N] output store; raw-2D I/O + exact signature kernel(x_tensor,w_tensor,eps,z_tensor,g_tensor)

decision: CLOSED -- do NOT explore. Off-PE transpose to remove the 512 identity-matmul transposes.
rationale: Both siblings closed this (BL-20260709-offpe-transpose-hidden-under-pe-floor): SBUF->SBUF dma_transpose of a [128,128] tile is infeasible (HW-DGE needs src.shape[0]==16, SW-DGE needs an HBM source -- shape/memory block), and nc_transpose(vector) lands in fp32 PSUM needing a re-cast and MEASURED +2% regress on the siblings. The 512 identity-matmul transposes (~27us PE-active) are already HIDDEN under the PE-bound matmul, so removing them changes nothing on the wall clock.

decision: FORBIDDEN this phase -- any precision / product-count change. The 3-product bf16 arithmetic is PINNED.
rationale: rel-L2 margin is 1.30x (v2 1.544749e-5 vs 2e-5 gate); the 4-product v2b was already a decision-SKIP (worst 1.5447e-5 < 1.8e-5 danger band; offline the 4th product moves rel-L2 only 4.454e-6->3.491e-6 for ~+25% PE, sibling v3b MEASURED-REJECT +28%); plain bf16 fails the gate ~117x. Phase 3 optimizes the SCHEDULE around the fixed 3-product arithmetic, not the arithmetic. See BL-20260709-compensated-bf16x2-split-beats-fp32-floor and the matmul_add_rmsnorm_v2b_4product_skip node.

decision: CLOSED -- do NOT implement. Split x into limbs BEFORE the transpose (wide [128,2048] limb ops) instead of per-transposed-sub-tile.
rationale: Splitting before transpose DOUBLES the transpose PE work: transpose x_hi and x_lo separately -> 32 transpose matmuls/M-tile instead of 16, adding PE-active -- the one thing a PE-bound kernel cannot afford. Phase 2 already fixed 'split AFTER the transpose costs one transpose, not two' (the exact fp32 identity transpose means splitting after == before, numerically). Adds cost with no benefit.
